── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 27, 37, 53, 40 mi
This week: 42 mi over 5 runs.
Feeling: "Anxious about the new date."
Asks: "The race got moved two weeks earlier, to October 18, because of the bridge works. That's three weeks from today. I've only done one 20. Do I still have time for my 22-miler?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: Skip the 22-miler: your 20 and last Sunday's 17 are enough, and the earlier race date makes this week the start of your taper. …
Answers: (1) No, I would not run a 22-miler, and you do not need one. … (2) You already have what a long run is for. … (3) The better use of this Sunday is 15 miles with the last 4 at marathon pace. It rehearses race effort on tired legs for a fraction of the recovery cost.
Next week:
Mon: rest. Full day off after Sunday's 17 miles; the taper starts here and rest is where…
Tue: easy, 6 mi, heart rate 135 to 142, flat or gently rolling, conversational. Keeps…
Wed: quality, 8 mi: 2 mi easy warm-up, 3 x 1.5 mi at 7:55 to 8:00/mi with 3 min easy jog…
Thu: easy, 5 mi, heart rate under 142, flat. One mile shorter than usual so the long run…
Fri: rest. Full rest before the last long run of the build.
Sat: easy, 4 mi, heart rate under 142, very relaxed, finish with 4 x 20 sec relaxed…
Sun: long, 15 mi, first 11 mi easy with heart rate under 148, then last 4 mi at marathon…
